# Results — Study 854 (Cash Conversion Cycle)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **a shortening
Cash Conversion Cycle (CCC = DSO + DIO − DPO) frees working capital, out-earns, and the stock
follows; a bloating CCC is a drag** (Richards-Laughlin 1980; Deloof 2003; the CFO/Hackett working-
capital scorecard tradition). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Prices fingerprint `d82e55a0af11` (yfinance daily adjusted closes);
events cache = 689 (ticker, filing) rows.*

**Fingerprint `d82e55a0af11`** · as-of **2026-06-30** · 30 names · 190 long-short months.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **30** large US filers (of a ~46-name price basket) with a long, cleanly-matched **five-fact** history on EDGAR — receivables, inventory, payables, revenue, COGS (fixed, current survivors; financials/REITs and pure-software excluded — they carry no inventory, so DIO/CCC is undefined) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: instants `AccountsReceivableNetCurrent`, `InventoryNet`, `AccountsPayableCurrent` + quarterly flows `Revenues` and `CostOfRevenue` (COGS fallback `CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold`), longest per-name history; de-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **689** CCC quarters, period ends **2009-07-31 → 2026-05-02**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 45 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `ccc_yoy_chg` = CCC(quarter) − CCC(same quarter a year earlier), in days, where CCC = DSO + DIO − DPO and each leg = balance ÷ (annualised quarterly flow ÷ 365). Ranked on `ccc_score = −ccc_yoy_chg` (high = shortening = long) |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, **long the shortening (falling-CCC) third / short the bloating (rising-CCC) third**, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** The CCC needs *five* matched facts per quarter (three balances +
two flows), each with its own tagging quirks (COGS is `CostOfRevenue` for some filers,
`CostOfGoodsAndServicesSold` for others; ASC-606 shifted revenue tags in 2018). Only **30** of the
~46-name basket expose a long clean history, and the matched cross-section **shrinks** over the
sample (≈16 names/month early, ≈12 late) — thinner even than the receivables-only sibling (853).
Terciles on a thin cross-section are noisy by construction. No survivorship correction: the basket
is current survivors — named on the Signal axis.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does a shortening CCC predict returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `ccc_score` (long shortening / short bloating), one
execution lag, 2010-09 → 2026-06 (**190 months**, avg cross-section 13.9 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **−47.1 bps/month** (−5.65%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | −1.37 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **−1.03** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | −0.34 |
| monthly hit rate | 47% (Wilson 95% CI [40%, 54%]) |
| long leg / short leg | +125.1 / +172.2 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×0.33 over 190 months |

The point estimate is **wrong-signed** — the falling-CCC (long) leg *under*-earns the rising-CCC
(short) leg, the opposite of the efficiency claim — but **statistically indistinguishable from zero**
(NW *t* = −1.03, one-sample −1.37). It is not even stably negative: the **staleness-120** cut is
−70.5 bps (NW *t* = −1.45) and the unit-free **percentage-change** signal `ΔCCC/CCC` is a flat
−2.8 bps (NW *t* = −0.07, Sharpe −0.02). There is no certifiable return predictability here in
either direction.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by signed score)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `ccc_score`; top-minus-bottom (shortening-minus-bloating)
forward drift, entered one day after the filing:

| horizon | n | top (shortening) | bottom (bloating) | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 687 | +1.25% | +1.00% | **+0.25%** | +0.40 | 52% | 0.34 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 681 | +4.26% | +4.59% | **−0.33%** | −0.27 | 53% | 0.62 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 676 | +8.43% | +8.19% | **+0.24%** | +0.09 | 52% | 0.46 |

Flat, and the sign **flips with the horizon** (positive at 1 month, negative at 1 quarter, positive
again at 2 quarters). The 63d tercile means are **non-monotone** (+4.59% / +3.33% / +4.26%,
bloating→shortening — a dip in the middle, and the shortening third does not top the bloating one),
the long-short *t* never exceeds +0.40, and the label-shuffle placebo *p* runs 0.34-0.62 — a random
tercile split matches or beats the real one about half the time. A horizon-dependent sign on a
non-monotone ladder is the signature of noise, not a signal.

## Era split — no regime rescues it (the sign flips)

Calendar long-short, split at 2018-01-01 (the ASC-606 revenue-tagging break):

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2010-2017 | 88 | +31.9 bps | +0.84 |
| 2018-2026 | 102 | −115.3 bps | −1.54 |

The signal is mildly **positive** (right-signed) before 2018 — but short of the bar at *t* = +0.84 —
and firmly **negative** (wrong-signed) after, *t* = −1.54. The full-sample negative is really a
post-2018 artefact, not a stable effect, and the modern half is both thinner (cross-section shrinks)
and the one dragging the sign the wrong way. There is no era in which this certifies in the claimed
direction.

## The mechanism — a shortening CCC precedes a wider margin only **faintly**

Pooled OLS of **next quarter's** gross-margin change on this quarter's CCC change (n = 487 matched
events):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| slope *b* | **−0.00010** (correctly negative) |
| *t* (iid-pooled) | −1.13 |
| R² | 0.003 |
| Pearson correlation | **−0.051** |
| next-q margin change, shortening tercile | **+0.40 pp** |
| next-q margin change, bloating tercile | **+0.13 pp** |
| tercile spread (shortening − bloating) | **+0.27 pp** |

The "frees cash → out-earns" mechanism is **present in the sign** — shortening-CCC names widen next
quarter's gross margin +0.27 percentage points more than bloating names, and the slope is correctly
negative — but **negligible in magnitude** (correlation −0.05, R² 0.003) and the pooled *t* (−1.13)
does not even clear 2 despite clustering. This is the study's *strongest* result and it is a whisper.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + signal panel with a TUNABLE planted lead (shortening-CCC names drift up); no
network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **+0.18** (sd 0.59), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **0/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 854) | **+18.07** (mean +907.2 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (zero crossings in twelve HAC *t*'s) and lights up hard on a
planted lead. The real-tape NW *t* = −1.03 is therefore a genuine null (a wrong-signed one), not a
broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a real-tape
stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly turnover
≈ 0.17):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | −54.6 bps/mo | −6.55%/yr | −1.19 | −0.40 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | −62.1 bps/mo | −7.45%/yr | −1.36 | −0.45 |

The gross edge was already wrong-signed and indistinguishable from zero; realistic friction only
deepens the loss. There is nothing to get paid for.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The forward-return long-short is **wrong-signed** (falling-CCC names *under*-earn
  rising-CCC names) and **statistically zero** (primary NW *t* = −1.03, one-sample −1.37), it does
  **not** survive perturbation (staleness-120 *t* = −1.45, percentage-change *t* = −0.07), the pooled
  event drift is **flat and sign-flipping** (long-short *t* +0.40 → −0.27 → +0.09; placebo *p*
  0.34-0.62), and the sign **flips across the 2018 break** (+0.84 → −1.54). No coherent, robust
  effect in the claimed direction — the desk's `NONE`. (One execution lag; survivorship named on the
  Signal axis; as-of 2026-06-30.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Not certifiable even gross (and wrong-signed); net of realistic
  long-short costs + borrow it is **−7.45%/yr** (*t* = −1.36, Sharpe −0.45). No paycheck.
- **"Does shortening the CCC precede a better margin?" — FAINT.** The mechanism is correctly signed
  (slope −0.00010, +0.27 pp shortening-minus-bloating future-margin spread) but economically
  negligible (correlation −0.05, R² 0.003). Real in direction, a whisper in size — not the lever the
  efficiency story promises.

> On big, liquid, heavily-covered names, shortening the cash conversion cycle is a real-but-tiny hint
> about next quarter's margin and — as far as this tape can tell — no usable hint at all about the
> stock.
